Marcus Blackmore And The Vitamins Empire Built On Stock
sum: Brookvale, on Sydney’s northern beaches, is not where you’d expect a listed pharmaceutical company’s roots to sit. But that’s where Maurice Blackmore set up a naturopathy clinic in the 1930s, selling herbal remedies out the back to patients who trusted him more than their doctors. His son Marcus joined the business in 1964, not as an heir with a strategy, but as a 21-year-old who’d failed his first attempt at university and needed somewhere to be useful. Sixty years later the company that grew from that shopfront, Blackmores, carries a market value that at its peak topped $2 billion. The story in between is less about vision and more about someone who stuck around long enough to get the timing right, twice.

I’ve spent a fair bit of time this year going back through old annual reports from companies that are still household names, and Blackmores is one of the stranger ones. It survived the 1970s as a fringe operation selling fish oil and wheatgerm to a market that barely existed. It survived a near-death stock crisis in the early 2000s that almost nobody outside the industry remembers now. And it survived, more recently, a collapse in Chinese demand that wiped out the better part of its share price inside eighteen months. None of that reads like genius. It reads like a business that kept showing up.

Maurice Blackmore was, by most accounts, a difficult man to work for and an even harder one to satisfy. He ran his clinic on a conviction that mainstream medicine had abandoned nutrition, and he built a small range of supplements to back that conviction up. When Marcus came into the business there was no grand plan for scale. The company incorporated formally in 1938 and limped along as a modest supplier to health food shops for decades, the kind of operation that existed because its founder believed in it, not because the market was clamouring for it.

What changed things wasn’t a single breakthrough product. It was distribution. Marcus Blackmore understood earlier than most in the natural health sector that pharmacies, not health food shops, were where the volume lived. Getting Blackmores products onto pharmacy shelves alongside Panadol and Codral gave the brand a legitimacy the industry hadn’t had before.

items.t: Vale stock: Cash flow supports outlook after Q3 earnings squeeze
sum: Vale released its third-quarter 2026 results on Thursday, October 29, with weaker iron ore economics weighing on profitability while copper and nickel operations provided support. The company's official Q3 2026 results release also added detail on costs, cash flow and metal-price realization.

Vale reported pro forma EBITDA of 3.5 billion US dollars for the quarter, down 20 percent from a year earlier and 14 percent from the previous quarter. The company attributed the decline mainly to lower realized iron ore fines prices, appreciation of the Brazilian real and higher bunker costs.

The average realized iron ore fines price fell to 85.1 US dollars per tonne, while iron ore C1 cash cost rose to 23.1 US dollars per tonne. All-in costs reached 60.4 US dollars per tonne, reflecting additional pressure from freight expenses.

Vale generated recurring free cash flow of 1.4 billion US dollars and total free cash flow of 2.2 billion US dollars in the quarter. Expanded net debt stood at 16.4 billion US dollars, 0.2 billion US dollars lower than in the previous quarter, as cash generation helped offset weaker EBITDA.

Iron ore sales increased 0.3 percent despite a 6 percent production decline. Copper sales fell 4 percent during the planned Sossego SAG mill rebuild, while nickel sales rose 16.1 percent. Vale reaffirmed its 2026 production guidance and expects copper and nickel output in the upper half of their respective ranges.

The company maintained its iron ore production guidance of 335 million to 345 million tonnes and expects full-year capital spending toward the lower end of its 5.4 billion to 5.7 billion US dollar range. Approval of the Salobo coarse particle flotation project adds a longer-term copper growth option based on existing infrastructure.

Vale stock holds 2026 guidance as iron ore weighs on Q3
sum: Vale's third-quarter results showed a sharp split across its metals portfolio. Iron ore earnings came under pressure from lower realized prices and higher external costs, while copper and nickel operations gained momentum. The company kept its 2026 production guidance intact.

In its 3Q26 Quarterly Results, Vale reported Proforma EBITDA of 3.5 billion US dollars for the July-to-September period, down 20 percent from a year earlier and 14 percent from the second quarter. The decline was mainly linked to weaker iron ore fines prices, a stronger Brazilian real and higher bunker costs.

The average realized iron ore fines price fell 10 percent year over year and quarter over quarter to 85.1 US dollars per tonne. Iron ore C1 cash costs rose 12 percent year over year to 23.1 US dollars per tonne, while all-in costs climbed 21 percent to 60.4 US dollars per tonne.

Iron ore production dropped 6 percent year over year, but sales increased 0.3 percent as Vale sold inventory accumulated in earlier periods. Pellet production rose 7 percent. The company attributed the lower iron ore output mainly to reduced run-of-mine availability at Serra Norte, partly offset by a quarterly production record at Serra Sul and additional volumes from the Capanema and Vargem Grande projects.

Vale Base Metals provided a counterweight. Realized copper prices increased to 15,314 US dollars per tonne, up 56 percent year over year, while nickel sales rose 16.1 percent. Copper sales were lower because of the planned Sossego SAG mill rebuild, but management said copper and nickel production remained on track for the upper half of their 2026 guidance ranges.

CEO Gustavo Pimenta said the company's freight strategy and hedging program helped protect margins in a dynamic market. Vale also highlighted the Serra Sul +20 project and the Compact Crushing project, which are intended to improve S11D performance. The company said October daily production at Serra Norte was already 15 percent higher, supporting its expectation of a stronger finish to the year.

Vale reaffirmed all 2026 production targets and said it remained confident of reaching the lower end of its iron ore guidance. Full-year capital expenditure is expected near the lower end of the 5.4 billion to 5.7 billion US dollar range.

Brazil stocks slide after Lula's election win; Petrobras leads Quant-rated holdings
sum: Brazilian stocks plunged after President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva secured a fourth term in Sunday's presidential runoff, defeating right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro and overturning market expectations of a shift toward more conservative economic policies.
The iShares MSCI Brazil ETF EWZ fell more than 27% in premarket trading on Monday as investors unwound positions built around a potential Bolsonaro victory.

Shares of oil major Petróleo Brasileiro S.A. - Petrobras PBR also tumbled, while banking stocks including Itaú Unibanco Holding S.A. ITUB and Banco Bradesco S.A. BBD came under heavy selling pressure.

The selloff followed a rally in Brazilian assets after Bolsonaro unexpectedly led the first round of voting earlier this month. Investors had anticipated that a change in political leadership could bring tighter fiscal policies, corporate tax reform and potential privatizations, helping contain government debt and eventually lower borrowing costs.

The strengthening Brazilian real had also supported sentiment by potentially easing inflationary pressures and attracting foreign capital. Lula's victory reversed those expectations, while Bolsonaro's refusal to concede and his challenge to the election result added to political uncertainty.
Against this backdrop, Seeking Alpha's Quant Ratings provide a snapshot of the fundamentals of major companies in the iShares MSCI Brazil ETF.

Petróleo Brasileiro S.A. - Petrobras leads the ranking, with its PBR shares earning a Strong Buy rating of 4.97 and its PBR.A shares following closely at 4.96. B3 S.A. - Brasil, Bolsa, Balcão BOLSY, Brazil's stock exchange operator, ranks third with a rating of 4.88, while Banco Bradesco rounds out the top four at 4.74. All four carry bullish ratings under the quantitative system.

Sigma Lithium Shares Jump 5.9% as Brazilian Court Restores Grota do Cirilo Environmental Licences

Sigma Lithium's stock climbed 5.9% during Wednesday pre-market activity in New York after a Brazilian appellate court affirmed the environmental permits for its principal Grota do Cirilo lithium project, allowing mining and processing to begin again.

The federal appeals panel reversed a September emergency ruling that had halted those permits amid litigation brought by Ngolo, an organization purporting to speak for nearby Quilombola populations. According to the court, an extended closure would inflict substantial and enduring economic damage across the Vale do Jequitinhonha area in Minas Gerais state.

This ruling eliminates a near-term legal hurdle for Grota do Cirilo, regarded as one of the planet's biggest and richest hard-rock lithium resources, while Sigma pursues an annualized output of 330,000 tonnes of lithium oxide concentrate by the close of 2027.

According to Sigma, the 2027 objective is attainable without expanding capacity, drawing on its current Mine 1 South Pit and Cleantech Industrial Plant. Following a technology enhancement during 2024's fourth quarter, the plant achieved daily production exceeding 950 tonnes, the company reported, with some days surpassing 1,000 tonnes.

With operations at its core asset having been disrupted by the legal battle, the resumption refocuses attention on Sigma's capacity to increase output. Meeting the projected growth through already-installed infrastructure might reduce the extra capital needed to fulfill its 2027 target.

After Huge Rally, Here’s How We’re Trading Brazilian Stocks
sum: Brazil is home to the largest stock market in Latin America. Boosted by an election held this past weekend, Brazilian stocks are gaining traction.

Earlier this year, we disclosed our long position in the iShares MSCI Brazil ETF (EWZ). EWZ contains familiar Brazilian names like Petrobras (PBR) and Vale SA (VALE). The position sat quietly for most of the year.

Then came this past weekend’s Brazilian elections. Incumbent President Lula (45.16%) was beaten by challenger Flavio Bolsonaro (47.03%). The result isn’t final, and will be determined by a runoff election on October 25.

Bolsonaro is favored to win that runoff, because it eliminates three candidates that received about 7.25% of the combined vote. The political platforms of all three candidates are considered closer to Bolsonaro than Lula, so eliminating them from the competition favors Bolsonaro.

I don’t know much about Brazilian politics, but I know the market likes this result. Our EWZ position shot higher by 12% on Monday, to reach a six-year high. EWZ has now gained 20% over the past week, and is up 34% year-to-date.
The move occurred on the ETF’s highest volume this year, an indication that this rally could have staying power (arrow).
Some of Brazil’s most popular individual names participated in the rally. ADRs for Petrobras Brasieiro SA jumped 13%. Petrobras closed at its highest level in 14 years.

Best Nickel Stocks in 2026 and How to Invest in Them
sum: Nickel stocks are shares of companies that produce, refine, or trade nickel, a metal with growing importance in global manufacturing. Nickel is best known as a key ingredient in stainless steel, but it's also used in electroplating, semiconductors, and rechargeable batteries.

After surging in the years following the COVID-19 lockdowns, nickel prices fell sharply in early 2025, briefly hitting a five-year low before stabilizing later in the year. Even so, nickel's role in high-growth industries, particularly electric vehicles, continues to attract long-term investor interest. EV batteries rely heavily on nickel-rich cathodes, making future demand closely tied to the pace of electrification.

That combination of cyclical pricing and long-term demand growth makes nickel stocks potentially attractive, but not without risk. Mining is capital-intensive, prices can be volatile, and geopolitical disruptions can affect supply. For investors willing to look beyond short-term swings, nickel stocks remain worth a closer look.
With those dynamics in mind, here are four nickel stocks that offer exposure to the metal and its long-term demand drivers.

Switzerland-based Glencore is a global metal mining giant. It's involved with energy production, recycling, agricultural products, and mining assets. Its operations include copper, cobalt (another resource used in EV batteries), and nickel mines. Glencore is one of the world's top producers of nickel, with mines in Canada, Norway, and Australia. The company reported nickel production of 35,800 metric tons in the first half of 2026.

For investors in the United States, bear in mind that Glencore is not directly listed on a U.S. stock exchange. Glencore is listed on the London Stock Exchange, but its shares can be purchased in the U.S. over the counter (OTC). There are certain risks involved in owning shares of a company like this.

While Glencore hasn't generated the same lofty profit margins as peers like BHP Group (BHP +1.37%) and the dividend hasn't grown much over the past decade, Glencore stock offered a 2.1% forward yield as of mid-September 2026, double the S&P 500's average yield.

items.t: Exporters make up half of September’s stock picks
sum: Financial sector is second most recommended by analysts while utilities lose ground

After the stock exchange ended August with a slightly negative performance of 0.33%, analysts’ stock-buying recommendations for September remain cautious, yet nearly half of Valor’s portfolio of stock picks has changed. Vale shares continue to lead the recommendations, but the company also has Petrobras keeping it company rather than Embraer. Both are recommended by six firms. Exporters gained ground in the rankings and are now the preferred sector, while utilities have fallen out of favor.

Analysts assess that Petrobras continues to post solid operating and financial results, in an environment of rising production and highly competitive oil extraction costs. And Vale has shown resilience in a challenging environment, says Régis Chinchila, chief investment analyst at Terra Investimentos.

Exporters account for half of the recommendations. Besides Petrobras and Vale, the group includes Embraer and newcomers Suzano and WEG, with three recommendations each. Ágora rates Suzano as buy based on the view that there is limited downside risk for pulp prices, with China showing signs of increased purchasing. Terra Investimentos says WEG posted a solid balance sheet last quarter.

The second most popular sector is financials, with two names: Itaú, with five recommendations, and B3, suggested by three firms—also one of September’s newcomers. Even though Itaú’s R$12.4 billion profit in the second quarter came in slightly below consensus, Andbank recommends the stock on the view that the bank’s asset quality remains intact.

“Even though this year is seen as a transition period with few short-term catalysts, Itaú remains well positioned,” says Fernando de Almeida Prado Bresciani, an analyst at Andbank. And B3 combines an “almost monopolistic” position in Brazilian capital markets infrastructure with strong cash generation, says Ricardo França, an analyst at Ágora.

In the fuel distribution segment, Ultrapar remains in the portfolio with three recommendations, but Vibra dropped out. Direcional entered as a “spicier pick” in the portfolio, replacing mall operator Multiplan.

Sdiptech acquires UK-based VALE Engineering
sum: Sdiptech AB (publ) has acquired 91 per cent of the shares in VALE Engineering (York) Ltd. The company has 15 employees and annual revenue of approximately GBP 5 million, with good profitability. The acquisition strengthens Sdiptech’s offering in road maintenance within the Supply Chain & Transportation business area.

Founded in 1999, VALE develops and manufactures specialist equipment for the maintenance of roads, public spaces and other infrastructure. Its largest product area is winter maintenance, including equipment for spreading salt for de-icing and snow ploughs. The company also offers professional weed-control equipment, as well as sports turf maintenance machinery.

The company serves customers across both the public and private sectors, including local authorities, infrastructure contractors and organisations responsible for large facilities. The business is primarily focused on the UK market, with some international exports.

“VALE has established a strong position in the UK market, with competitive and highly specialised products. Its solutions contribute to safer and more efficient maintenance of roads and public spaces. The acquisition of VALE further strengthens our offering in road maintenance and complements our existing operations within Supply Chain & Transportation well,” says Daniel Unge, Head of Supply Chain & Transportation.

“VALE designs and manufactures machines that solve real-world problems. Over the years, we have developed a strong portfolio of specialist products and built a trusted name associated with quality, reliability and ease of use. I’m particularly proud that, together with my family and the entire VALE team, we have built a successful business where our products are designed, engineered and manufactured here in York. Sdiptech’s culture and long-term approach align well with our values,” says James Wilson, Managing Director of VALE.
The aquisition will be included in the Supply Chain & Transportation business area as of September 2026 and the management team will stay the same following the acquisition.

items.t: Vale shares rise as China replenishes iron ore stocks
sum: Vale shares rise amid iron ore restocking in China — The Rio Times

American depositary receipts of Brazilian mining company Vale rose 2.53% on August 21, closing at $14.59. CSN Mineração shares in São Paulo gained 4.80% to 5.90 Brazilian reals, while Rio Tinto’s U.S.-listed securities increased 3.06% to $105.30.

The rise in iron ore producers’ quotations occurred despite the nearly unchanged price of the commodity itself. The iron ore benchmark ended trading at $95.21 per tonne, only 0.05% above the previous level, The Rio Times reports.

Iron ore inventories at 35 major Chinese ports decreased by 1.24 million tonnes over the week, to 145.54 million tonnes as of August 21. The average daily volume of shipments from ports increased by 48,000 tonnes, reaching 3.136 million tonnes.

The Rio Times interprets these figures as evidence that Chinese steelmakers continued withdrawing ore from stockpiles to replenish inventories. China imports about 75% of all seaborne iron ore, so port inventory dynamics are an important indicator for the market.

In the first seven months of 2026, China increased ore imports by 6%, to 736.84 million tonnes. At the same time, the country’s crude steel production declined by about 3% in the first half of the year, to 499.95 million tonnes.

In July, steel output amounted to 76.93 million tonnes, 3.6% less than a year earlier. This was the lowest figure for July since 2017. According to the publication, demand in the construction sector remains weak, while steel inventories are rising.

Vale Q2 Earnings Call Spotlights Copper Growth and Cost Reset
sum: Vale S.A. VALE used its second-quarter 2026 earnings call to emphasize faster copper development, execution and shareholder returns, while acknowledging a higher iron ore cost base tied to currency, oil and freight assumptions.

Earnings of 36 cents per share missed the Zacks Consensus Estimate of 41 cents by 12.20%. Revenues of $10.49 billion topped the consensus estimate of $10.40 billion by 0.90%, but management focused the call on forward priorities.
VALE S.A. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | VALE S.A. Quote

Marcelo Bacci, executive vice president of finance and investor relations, raised 2026 iron ore C1 cash cost guidance to $22.50-$23.50 per ton from $20-$21.50. He cited a stronger Brazilian real, higher diesel prices and inventory effects.
Bacci also lifted all-in cost guidance to $58-$62 per ton from $52-$56. The range assumes Brent crude at $86 per barrel and an exchange rate of 5.13 Brazilian reais per dollar.

The offset came from base metals. Bacci lowered copper all-in cost guidance to $0-$500 per ton and nickel guidance to $10,000-$11,500 per ton, citing operating improvements and stronger by-product economics.

Gustavo Pimenta, chief executive officer, said Bacaba is scheduled to start commissioning in the third quarter of 2027, ahead of the prior first-half 2028 timetable. The 50,000-ton project was 39% complete at quarter-end.

53-unit tower planned for Mona Vale under fast-tracked proposal
sum: A seven-storey apartment block is proposed for Sydney’s northern beaches, with plans to fast track it past local council under the “state significant development” scheme.
The 53 apartment project, dubbed Dawn will be built in a predominantly low-rise area of Mona Vale and involve the demolition of an existing block of 18 apartments.
The new apartments will be two- to three-bedrooms and nine of the apartments on level one will be build-to-rent.
Josh Thompson is the managing director for the developer, Inca Property Group, and said the group were “conscious” of the potential community impact.
“It is important to us that Dawn contributes affordable housing as part of the development,” Mr Thompson said.
“Given its proximity to the hospital, schools and shopping centre, this is an accessible location for key workers, small business owners and employees to call home,” he said.
The developer is seeking a “State Significant Development Application” that will speed up the approval process.

Brazil Export Stocks Facing New US Tariff Pressure
sum: The new U.S. tariffs of up to 37.5% on thousands of Brazilian exports are reshaping the risk profile for several Brazil focused stocks exposed to sugar, ethanol, pig iron, wood products, and tobacco. For investors weighing how this trade shock might influence portfolios, the opportunity is less about chasing a theme and more about deciding which companies carry tariff heavy U.S. exposure that could pressure future sales and margins. This article walks through 3 stocks that appear on the US Tariff Impact Stocks With High Brazil Export Exposure screener and that look more vulnerable under the latest trade measures.

Overview: Suzano is a Brazilian pulp and paper producer that sells eucalyptus based pulp, printing and writing papers, packaging board and tissue products across Brazil and international markets, while also expanding into biofuels, power generation and cellulose based consumer goods.
Operations: Suzano generates most of its revenue from Pulp at about R$37.6b, with a smaller but meaningful contribution from Paper at roughly R$12.0b.

Investors looking at Suzano have to weigh an apparently cheap stock against rising risks from the new U.S. tariffs and a business model that leans heavily on debt funded returns. The company sits at the center of Brazilian wood products and pulp exports. Higher duties on wood moldings and paper exports to the U.S. could pressure volumes or pricing, even as management tries to shift product to other regions and pass on a prior 10% tariff to customers. Earnings forecasts already point to weaker growth ahead and interest costs are not comfortably covered, so any hit to cash flow from trade friction, integration challenges in U.S. packaging assets or new mineral projects could leave Suzano looking less like a bargain than headline valuation suggests.
